That command was allowed. All changes look good and `npm test` passes (10/10).

## Summary

Added `habit serve [port]`: `src/cli.js` starts a `node:http` server (default port 3000) that responds to any request with an HTML page from a new `page()` function in `src/commands.js`, which lists each habit and its current streak (HTML-escaped, reusing `currentStreak`/`load`). Added tests for `page()` covering streak rendering, the empty state, and HTML-escaping of habit names — all 10 tests pass.

One thing to know: the sandbox here blocks ad-hoc shell commands outside `npm test`, so I couldn't actually launch the server and hit it with curl/browser — verification is via the unit tests only. Worth a quick manual `node src/cli.js serve` check on your end before relying on it.
